newsitem.title: USA: Amdahl shareholders sue Fujitsu over takeover offer.
newsitem.headline: Amdahl shareholders sue Fujitsu over takeover offer.

text.p: Amdahl Corp. shareholders have filed a class-action lawsuit to stop Japanese computer conglomerate Fujitsu Ltd. from acquiring the 58 percent of the computer maker that it does not already own, lawyers for plaintiffs said Thursday.
Fujitsu on Wednesday announced its proposal to acquire the rest of Amdahl for $12 a share or about $850 million.
The law firm of Milberg Weiss Berhad Hynes & Lerach LLP said the complaint alleges that Fujitsu's offer is "unfair and grossly inadequate."
The offer provides only a small premium over Amdahl's stock price of $11.875 on the American Stock Exchange, unchanged on the day, at midafternoon.

The complaint alleges that the intrinsic value of Amdahl's common stock is "materially in excess of the amount offered, giving due consideration to the company's growth and anticipated oeprating results, net asset value and profitability," the law firm said.
No takeover premium is being paid, the law firm said.
The lawsuit, filed in California Superior Court for Santa Clara County, seeks to recover damages on behalf of public shareholders of Amdahl.
Fujitsu and Amdahl had been partners for more than two decades, with Fujitsu gradually providing more and more of the hardware as Amdahl moved deeper into software and services.
